- Inner pod walls show brownish discoloration with distinct darker spots
- Whitish/pale material visible on the inner pod walls — looks like a dried, crusty substance

**Comparing to references:**
- **White_Mold**: External fluffy mold on pods/stem — doesn't match (test image shows internal pod view, no external fluffy growth)
- **Phomopsis**: Dry shriveled dark seeds with gray mold — doesn't match (test seeds are green/fresh)
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Composition very similar (opened pod held by hand) but test image has no purple seed staining
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus**: Mottled/black-marked seeds — doesn't match
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Dark external pod discoloration — doesn't match
- **Phytophthora**: Pod on dying plant — doesn't match

The whitish crusty material coating the inside of the pod walls + brown inner-wall lesions + green seeds best aligns with **Downy_mildew**, whose KB explicitly states: *"Inside of infected pods and seeds may be covered with a dried, whitish fungal mass that appears crusty."* No other pod-relevant candidate accounts for the white internal coating alongside otherwise-green seeds. Though Downy mildew is indexed under "leaf" in the part index, the disease is known to infect pod interiors, and no other candidate explains the full visual pattern.
